newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close sharply higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close sharply higher in active trade.

text.p: Delhi shares ended sharply higher on strong buying, triggered by reports that the bourse regulator, Security and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), might introduce a liberal carry-forward trading system, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 14.34 points higher at 879.95.

Brokers said the buying sentiment was helped by a report in the Economic Times newspaper that a committee formed to look into the carry-forward system of stock trading had made favourable recomendations.
"If the J.S. Verma committee recomends a market friendly revised carry-forword trading system, then the market should witness a bull phase," said stock brokers.
Reliance Industries ended 2.75 rupees higher at 349.25 on speculative purchases.
TISCO rose 10.20 rupees or nearly 5 percent to 212.45 rupees on strong buying by foreign institutional investors, brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 4.50 rupees to 330.50 rupees on foreign buying.
Larsen and Toubro climbed 11.60 rupees to 269.00.
ACC gained 58.50 rupees or 3.9 percent to 1,528.00 rupees on speculative buying.
